title: Maple Cricket League streetwear brand pack: grade six mixed-light street-cricket frames to one house look off in-frame grey cards, trace the logo system, burn the away crest to a one-colour print separation, and cut the merch
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brand-identity brief for an invented streetwear-forward backyard/street-cricket league aimed at the South Asian and Caribbean diaspora in a large North American metro. The client name is the fictional 'Maple Cricket League' (MCL); no real brand, label, league, franchise, team, athlete, school, or third-party product is named or depicted anywhere in a task-facing field. Aesthetic references are kept generic ('elevated diaspora-streetwear and franchise-cricket look') rather than naming real labels. The connector's own operations are described in the brief only as generic craft terms (a colour-grade, a vector trace, a one-colour print burn, a knockout) so the brief states GOALS, not tool names. REASONABLY ENRICHED to make the chain concrete, failable and measurable, and to repair the earlier single-hero version flagged in audit groups G3 (repetition/plumbing sold as difficulty) and G5 (wrong tool for the stated craft): the brand-photography deliverable is restored from ONE hero to a batch of SIX frames shot across different sessions under deliberately different light (warm dusk street light, cool overcast, greenish indoor net cage, warm golden-hour rooftop, cool open shade, hard midday sun), each carrying an in-frame neutral 18% grey card + white chip so the set can be reconciled to one house white point after the fact; a photographed embroidered cap patch is added as a triage decoy that looks like 'another logo image' but must NOT be traced; and the stale 'AI-outpaint the banner to extended canvas' language from the prior version is fully removed in favour of an honest gen-free crop reframe. No out-of-scope deliverable (website, written copy, social templates, from-scratch logo design) is invented; the pack is scoped to the connector-doable production-art thread.
one_line_ask: Reconcile six differently-lit street-cricket frames to one house streetwear look using their in-frame grey cards (each frame a different correction to the same target, reported as applied settings), author the hero and reframe it into a wide header, trace the flat logo-system art into clean vector, export the client's authored vector master for the factory, burn the tilted away crest into a one-colour print separation, and cut out the jersey and cap for the lookbook.
full_brief:
Maple Cricket League (MCL) is a streetwear-forward street/backyard cricket league for the diaspora community. The identity is already designed; we need the production-art thread executed and handed back as clean, organised, correctly named files. Our own team handles the website, the written brand voice and the social templates — do NOT build those here.

What we are sending you:
• Six brand photos of our street-cricket sessions. Fair warning: they were shot on different days in very different light and they do NOT match out of camera — some warm, some cold, some flat, some contrasty. On the edge of every frame the shooter left a neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip so the set can be brought to a common white balance after the fact. One of them also came in a few degrees off level.
• A flat scan of the logo-system art sheet (crest + monogram + hat badge laid out together, two flat ink colours on paper).
• Our authored multi-artboard vector master of those same three marks, already built and ready to hand to the factory.
• A photo of the away-kit chest crest — one dark ink on near-white fabric — that came in slightly rotated and off-centre.
• A studio flat of a folded home jersey on a seamless sweep, and a close photo of the embroidered crest patch on a cap.

The bar (this is the whole job):
1. BRAND PHOTOGRAPHY — the six frames have to read as ONE brand. Every frame must resolve to the SAME house look: the neutral grey card in each lands truly neutral (no residual warm or cool cast) at one common white point, the shadows sit on one common deep-but-not-crushed near-black floor that never clips a channel to zero, the palette pulled toward a muted, filmic street tone with skin kept alive and speculars held. Because the frames start from different casts and exposures, each one needs a DIFFERENT correction to hit that shared target — a set that is each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will not agree at the grey cards and we will reject it. Author the look on the strongest frame first, then match the rest to it. Level the crooked frame. Hand back a short sheet listing, per frame, the white balance / exposure / black-point you dialed, so we can confirm the set was matched to one target and not eyeballed frame by frame. Then give us the strongest frame reframed into a wide site/social HEADER, using the room already in the shot, with clean empty space on one side for a headline — no invented canvas.
2. LOGO SYSTEM — turn the flat art sheet into clean, infinitely-scalable vector artwork, and separately export our authored vector master to a print-ready vector file (plus a raster preview) for the factory. Do not redraw or reinvent the marks.
3. AWAY CREST PRINT — turn the away-kit crest into a one-colour, print-ready screen/sublimation separation at print resolution: get it square and level, cropped tight to the print bounds, and rendered as a single-ink treatment the factory can burn.
4. MERCH CUT-OUTS — give us clean transparent cut-outs of the folded jersey and of the cap for the lookbook / e-commerce.

Hard rules: no inventing new artwork, no from-scratch logo or lettering, no generative fill or canvas extension, no compositing one image onto another. The vector master export must come from the authored master file we supply. Every step after each asset loads must build on a previous result.

inputs.name: brand_01_dusk_laneway.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Candid documentary photograph of young South Asian and Caribbean men playing street cricket in an urban laneway at dusk, one batter mid-swing with a taped tennis ball, friends fielding, elevated streetwear fits (oversized tees, caps, layered fits), brick walls and chain-link behind. Lit mainly by warm sodium/tungsten street lighting (~3000K, strong warm amber cast), slightly underexposed and flat straight out of camera, the whole frame tilted about 4 degrees clockwise so the ground line is not level. A neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip clipped to a fence at the far LEFT edge of the frame as a white-balance reference. Real skin pores, individual flyaway hairs, natural sensor grain, faint motion in the bat, no CGI gloss, shot like a real 35mm reportage frame. 4000x2670.
inputs.realism_notes: THE HERO and the frame that DEFINES the house look. Deliberately WARM (sodium ~3000K), underexposed and tilted ~4deg CW, so it needs a real straighten, a cool-ward white balance to drive its grey card neutral, and an exposure lift — all reasoned by eye. The grey/white reference sits at the FAR LEFT so it survives into the retained graded master (grader measures neutrality there) yet is cropped OUT when the batter is offset right for the wide header. Camera-scale 4000px so the 1920x640 header is an honest downscale, never an upscale. This frame's dialed settings become the shared target the other five must match; its own correction must NOT be copied verbatim onto the others.

inputs.name: brand_02_overcast_pitch.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Candid documentary photograph of a street-cricket pitch on an overcast afternoon, bowler running in on a cracked asphalt lane, streetwear-clad fielders, muted grey sky. Cool flat overcast light (~6300K, mild blue-grey cast), a touch bright and low in contrast straight out of camera. A neutral 18% grey card and small white chip resting on a kit bag at the edge of the frame. Real fabric and skin texture, natural grain, documentary realism, no CGI. 4000x2670.
inputs.realism_notes: COOL + flat + slightly bright frame. The correct move toward the shared target is the OPPOSITE of the hero: WARM the white balance to neutralise its grey card, pull exposure DOWN a little, add contrast to seat the house black-floor. Copying the hero's cool/lift numbers here leaves it cold and bright and breaks the match — part of the divergent-per-frame trap. Not tilted.

inputs.name: brand_03_net_cage.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Candid documentary photograph inside an indoor practice net cage, a batter shadow-driving under overhead fluorescent tubes, netting and concrete around. Dim greenish fluorescent light (~4200K with a distinct green/magenta imbalance), underexposed. A neutral 18% grey card and white chip hanging on the netting at the frame edge as reference. Real net texture, skin detail, sensor grain, no CGI gloss. 4000x2670.
inputs.realism_notes: The GREEN-CAST frame. Needs a tint (green->magenta) correction that neither the warm nor the cool frames need, plus an exposure lift, to bring its grey card to true neutral at the shared white point. A pure temperature move (no tint) leaves a green cast that a naive one-axis white balance misses — an invisible-until-you-look-at-the-card failure. Not tilted.

inputs.name: brand_04_golden_rooftop.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Candid documentary photograph of a rooftop street-cricket knock-around at golden hour, low warm sun raking across the players, city skyline soft behind, streetwear fits glowing. Strong warm low-sun light (~3400K, warm cast), bright with hot highlights on skin and caps. A neutral 18% grey card and white chip on a ledge at the frame edge. Real skin and fabric micro-detail, natural grain, no CGI. 4000x2670.
inputs.realism_notes: WARM like the hero but BRIGHT with blown-risk highlights — so it needs the warm-to-neutral white balance AND a downward exposure nudge with highlight recovery, unlike the hero which is lifted. Two warm frames that still take different exposure moves. Its dialed numbers should be close to the hero's in hue but clearly different in exposure. Not tilted.

inputs.name: brand_05_open_shade.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Candid documentary photograph of players resting between overs in cool open shade beside a concrete wall, one spinning a ball, relaxed streetwear posture. Cool blue open-shade light (~7000K, clear blue cast), flat and slightly dim. A neutral 18% grey card and white chip propped against the wall at the frame edge. Real skin pores, fabric weave, sensor grain, documentary realism, no CGI. 4000x2670.
inputs.realism_notes: The COOLEST frame (open shade ~7000K). Needs the strongest WARM white-balance shift of the set and a modest lift to land its grey card neutral at the shared white point. If the same recipe used on the warm frames is applied here it stays blue — the divergent-correction gate. Not tilted.

inputs.name: brand_06_midday_sun.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Candid documentary photograph of a midday street-cricket match in hard direct sun, sharp shadows on the asphalt, a fielder diving, high contrast. Near-neutral but hot noon light (~5200K), very contrasty with bright highlights and deep shadows. A neutral 18% grey card and white chip on the kerb at the frame edge. Real skin, fabric and asphalt texture, natural grain, no CGI gloss. 4000x2670.
inputs.realism_notes: Near-neutral in HUE but the exposure/contrast problem child: hot highlights and crushed-risk shadows. Its white-balance move is small, but it needs highlight recovery and a lifted-but-controlled shadow to seat the SAME deep-not-clipped black-floor as the rest without losing the house contrast. Auto-tone would key off its own extreme histogram and diverge from the set. Not tilted.

inputs.name: logo_system_sheet.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat, slightly imperfect scan on off-white paper of a streetwear cricket-league logo SHEET: three marks of the same brand laid in a row — (1) a shield crest with two crossed cricket bats over a maple-leaf motif and the letters 'MCL', (2) a bold interlocking 'MCL' monogram, (3) a simplified maple-and-crossed-bats hat badge. Two flat ink colours only — deep forest green and cream. Faint paper texture, a slight scan shadow along one edge, marginally uneven ink. 3200x2000.
inputs.realism_notes: TRACEABLE source. Flat two-ink art on paper so a raster->vector trace produces clean, scalable paths with genuine edges. Faint paper margin/scan shadow means a crop-to-bounds prep before tracing is real work. This is one half of the triage pair with the cap-patch photo below: both are 'logo images', but only THIS flat art sheet is traceable — the patch photo is not.

inputs.name: logo_system_master.ai
inputs.gen_prompt: A genuine authored multi-artboard vector master file (.ai) containing three artboards — Artboard 1: MCL circular crest; Artboard 2: interlocking MCL monogram; Artboard 3: simplified hat badge — each as real vector paths on named layers (CREST, MONOGRAM, HAT_BADGE), two global swatches (forest green, cream), outlined type. This is the client's already-built master, ready to EXPORT to a print-ready vector file and a raster preview; it is NOT to be authored from scratch by the agent.
inputs.realism_notes: AUTHORED-INPUT vector master: the vector-document export tool only EXPORTS a genuine pre-existing .ai, it does not compose one. Real vector geometry across three artboards so a single combined export is meaningful. Distinct from the flat scan (logo_system_sheet.png): the sheet is traced to SVG, the master is exported to PDF/PNG — two different, legitimate paths, not a redundant pair.

inputs.name: away_crest_graphic.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat, head-on photograph of the MCL away-kit chest crest printed in a single dark ink on light cream fabric: the shield emblem with crossed cricket bats over a maple-leaf motif and the letters 'MCL'. The panel is rotated about 3 degrees and sits off-centre in the frame with surrounding cream fabric around it. Real woven fabric texture, even studio light. 3600x3600.
inputs.realism_notes: The one-colour PRINT-SEPARATION source. Intentionally ~3deg rotated and off-centre so a straighten (only the dedicated auto-straighten tool rectifies a tilt — the crop and tone tools cannot rotate) and a crop-to-bounds are genuine, dependent steps before the print burn. Single dark ink on near-white so the halftone burn yields a true single-ink separation. Camera-scale 3600px so a 300 DPI print-size separation is a downscale, never an upscale.

inputs.name: home_jersey_flat.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Studio e-commerce photograph of a neatly folded short-sleeve cricket jersey in deep forest green with the cream MCL shield crest on the chest, laid on a plain light-grey seamless paper sweep, soft even studio light, a soft contact shadow. Real knit fabric texture. 3000x3750.
inputs.realism_notes: Straightforward product cut-out source: plain seamless sweep with a clean subject edge so a background knockout to transparency yields a clean lookbook cut-out. Real fabric texture and a soft contact shadow keep it photographic. The knockout isolates the OUTER sweep only — no enclosed interior hole is claimed.

inputs.name: cap_patch_photo.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Close product photograph of an embroidered MCL crest patch stitched onto the front panel of a forest-green streetwear cap, raised satin-stitch thread with visible individual stitches, twill weave, soft fabric folds and specular sheen on the thread, on a plain light backdrop, soft studio light. 3000x3000.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE DECOY. It looks like 'another logo image' next to the flat art sheet, but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of raised embroidery on woven fabric — threads, folds, weave and sheen. Its only correct use is as the cap lookbook cut-out (knock the backdrop to transparency). Routed to the tracer like the flat art sheet it returns garbage thread/weave paths; the failure is invisible until the SVG path data is opened. The correct call is the same background-knockout used on the jersey — NOT the trace used on logo_system_sheet.png.

outputs.name: brand_01_dusk_graded_master.jpg
outputs.spec: Hero street-cricket frame straightened and graded to the authored MCL house look (grey card neutralised to the common white point; shadows on the common deep-but-unclipped near-black floor; muted filmic street palette; batter subject lifted off the surround via a masked local edit; fine grain). Full-frame graded MASTER with the in-frame grey/white reference RETAINED at the left edge — this is the archival house-look reference the grader measures neutrality on. sRGB JPEG, ~4000px long edge.

outputs.name: brand_02_overcast_graded_master.jpg
outputs.spec: Overcast frame graded to MATCH the house look at the common white point and black-floor via its OWN correction (a warm-ward, exposure-down move distinct from the hero's). Full-frame graded master, grey/white card retained in frame for the neutrality check. sRGB JPEG, ~4000px long edge.

outputs.name: brand_03_net_cage_graded_master.jpg
outputs.spec: Indoor net-cage frame graded to match the house look, its green/fluorescent cast neutralised (a tint correction the other frames do not need) so its grey card lands neutral at the common white point. Full-frame graded master, card retained. sRGB JPEG, ~4000px long edge.

outputs.name: brand_04_golden_graded_master.jpg
outputs.spec: Golden-hour frame graded to match the house look, warm-to-neutral white balance plus a downward exposure/highlight-recovery move (opposite exposure direction from the hero). Full-frame graded master, card retained. sRGB JPEG, ~4000px long edge.

outputs.name: brand_05_open_shade_graded_master.jpg
outputs.spec: Open-shade frame graded to match the house look, the strongest warm white-balance shift of the set to pull its blue cast to neutral at the common white point. Full-frame graded master, card retained. sRGB JPEG, ~4000px long edge.

outputs.name: brand_06_midday_graded_master.jpg
outputs.spec: Midday hard-sun frame graded to match the house look, a small white-balance move but highlight recovery and controlled shadow lift to seat the SAME black-floor as the set without losing house contrast. Full-frame graded master, card retained. sRGB JPEG, ~4000px long edge.

outputs.name: brand_header_wide.jpg
outputs.spec: Wide site/social HEADER (~1920x640, 3:1) reframed from the graded hero by an honest off-centre crop-and-resize of the existing frame: the batter offset to one side so the room already in the shot forms clean empty negative space on the other for a headline overlay. The grey/white reference card is cropped OUT of this deliverable (card-exclusion checked here, separately from the neutrality check on the retained master). Existing pixels only — no invented canvas, no upscale. sRGB JPEG.

outputs.name: brand_grade_report.txt
outputs.spec: A plain parameter sheet the agent authors and returns: for each of the six frames, the white-balance temperature and tint, the exposure offset, and the black-point value that were APPLIED, plus the single common house white point and near-black floor all six were matched to, and the straighten angle used on the hero. This is the acceptance artifact that makes 'matched to one target' checkable; the per-frame corrections must be NON-identical (warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed, the green frame tinted). It is an applied-settings log — not a measured/recovered pixel readout.

outputs.name: logo_system_traced.svg
outputs.spec: Clean scalable vector of the full logo system (crest + monogram + hat badge) traced from logo_system_sheet.png after a crop-to-bounds prep. Resolution-independent SVG with two flat fill colours (forest green + cream), tight continuous paths, no raster embeds; suitable for infinite scaling on apparel and print.

outputs.name: logo_master_export.pdf
outputs.spec: Print-ready vector export of the client's authored 3-artboard logo_system_master.ai (crest, monogram, hat badge, all artboards together), for the factory. Vector PDF (no rasterisation).

outputs.name: logo_master_preview.png
outputs.spec: Raster PNG preview of the authored logo master, exported by a SECOND vector-document export call (the export tool emits one media type per call), to accompany the vector PDF.

outputs.name: away_crest_screenprint_halftone.png
outputs.spec: Single-colour (one-ink) halftone screen/sublimation SEPARATION of the away-kit chest crest, straightened square and cropped tight to the print bounds, rendered as a single-ink halftone treatment the factory can burn. 300 DPI at print size (a downscale from the 3600px camera-scale source), one-colour dot pattern on white.

outputs.name: jersey_cutout.png
outputs.spec: Transparent-background product cut-out of the folded home jersey for the lookbook / e-commerce, produced by knocking out the seamless sweep. PNG with alpha, clean subject edge, subject preserved at source resolution, sRGB.

outputs.name: cap_patch_cutout.png
outputs.spec: Transparent-background product cut-out of the embroidered cap for the lookbook, produced by knocking out the plain backdrop. A RASTER PNG with alpha and NO vector paths — this file proves the cap photo was correctly triaged as a photograph to be cut out, not routed to the tracer. Subject preserved at source resolution, sRGB.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: brand_01_dusk_laneway.jpg, brand_02_overcast_pitch.jpg, brand_03_net_cage.jpg, brand_04_golden_rooftop.jpg, brand_05_open_shade.jpg, brand_06_midday_sun.jpg, logo_system_sheet.png, logo_system_master.ai, away_crest_graphic.jpg, home_jersey_flat.jpg, cap_patch_photo.jpg
connector_workflow.note: Single ingest of every client asset into the working project so all downstream steps run against real references. Plumbing only — not the difficulty; every later step consumes a named prior output.
BRAND-PHOTO BRANCH, hero. Level the off-level hero frame so the later off-centre header crop is measured against a true horizon. Report the correcting angle used.

AUTHOR the MCL house look on the hero and record it as the target the other five must hit. Working BY EYE off the in-frame grey/white card, dial temperature and tint until the card reads truly neutral, set exposure/contrast, hold the highlights, and set blacks so the shadows floor at a deep-but-unclipped near-black; pull the palette toward a muted, filmic street tone (reduced saturation with skin kept alive) using the adjustment primitives. This is a reasoned authored grade, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. Report the temperature/tint/exposure/black values chosen — they define the shared target. Consumes step 2.

Shape the streetwear palette with a per-hue-band HSL move: gently desaturate and darken the ambient environment hues and give skin a moderate, bounded warm-ward lift, all within a moderate range (no near-complementary hue rotation). Part of the authored look built from primitives, not a canned tint. Consumes step 3.
Semantic subject selection of the batter on the graded hero to drive a local lift; returns a mask URI. Consumes step 4.

Masked local edit: apply a small exposure/clarity lift to the batter subject ONLY, using the step-5 mask, so the subject reads off the surround while the house black-floor set in step 3 is left untouched. The adjustment tool accepts a mask, so this is a genuine local edit, not a whole-image push. Consumes step 4 image + step 5 mask.

Fine film grain to finish the house look. DELIVERABLE brand_01_dusk_graded_master.jpg — the full-frame graded hero MASTER with the grey/white card retained at the left edge (neutrality is graded here). Consumes step 6.

Grade the overcast frame to the SAME target set in step 3, reasoning its OWN correction from its own grey card and histogram (a distinct white-balance and exposure move, not the hero's numbers). Neutralise its grey card at the common white point and seat the common black-floor. Report the values applied. Consumes the uploaded overcast frame.
Same house grain finish as the hero. DELIVERABLE brand_02_overcast_graded_master.jpg, card retained. Consumes step 8.

Grade the net-cage frame to the shared target from its own card — this frame needs both temperature AND tint reasoning to bring its grey card fully neutral, plus an exposure move, then the common black-floor. Report the values applied. Consumes the uploaded net-cage frame.
House grain finish. DELIVERABLE brand_03_net_cage_graded_master.jpg, card retained. Consumes step 10.

Grade the golden-hour frame to the shared target from its own card: neutralise its warm cast and reason its exposure/highlight move independently, then seat the common black-floor. Report the values applied. Consumes the uploaded golden-hour frame.
House grain finish. DELIVERABLE brand_04_golden_graded_master.jpg, card retained. Consumes step 12.

Grade the open-shade frame to the shared target from its own card: the correction that lands its grey card neutral at the common white point (the largest warm-ward move of the set), plus a modest lift and the common black-floor. Report the values applied. Consumes the uploaded open-shade frame.
House grain finish. DELIVERABLE brand_05_open_shade_graded_master.jpg, card retained. Consumes step 14.

Grade the midday hard-sun frame to the shared target from its own card: a small white-balance move but highlight recovery and a controlled shadow lift so it floors at the SAME near-black as the set without losing house contrast. Report the values applied. Consumes the uploaded midday frame.
House grain finish. DELIVERABLE brand_06_midday_graded_master.jpg, card retained. Consumes step 16.

OWNED DESIGN ENDPOINT. Reframe the graded hero MASTER into the wide ~1920x640 header by an honest off-centre crop-and-resize: place the batter to one side so the room already in the shot forms clean headline negative space on the other, and crop the left-edge reference card OUT in the same move. Existing pixels only from the 4000px master — no invented canvas, no upscale. DELIVERABLE brand_header_wide.jpg. Consumes step 7.

LOGO BRANCH, prep-before-trace. Crop the flat logo art sheet to the tight bounds of the three marks, dropping the paper margin and the scan-shadow edge so the trace sees only the artwork. Consumes the uploaded logo sheet.
Raster->SVG trace of the cropped two-ink art sheet into clean scalable paths (forest green + cream as separate fills). DELIVERABLE logo_system_traced.svg. Consumes step 19.

EXPORT the client's authored 3-artboard vector master (.ai) to a print-ready vector PDF, all artboards together, for the factory. The export tool only EXPORTS a genuine pre-existing master; it does not author one. It emits ONE media type per call, so the raster preview is a separate call (next). Consumes the uploaded logo_system_master.ai.
Second export call: render the same authored vector master to a raster PNG preview that accompanies the vector PDF (one media type per call). Consumes the uploaded logo_system_master.ai.

AWAY-CREST PRINT BRANCH. Square the ~3deg rotation of the crest panel before cropping and burning — only the dedicated straighten tool rectifies a tilt; the crop and tone tools cannot rotate, so a skipped straighten leaves a crooked screen. Consumes the uploaded away crest.
Crop tight to the crest's print bounds, removing the surrounding cream fabric so the separation is exactly the artwork to be burned. Consumes step 23.

Burn the straightened, cropped single-ink crest to a one-colour halftone screen/sublimation separation for the factory. DELIVERABLE away_crest_screenprint_halftone.png at 300 DPI print size. Consumes step 24.

MERCH BRANCH. Knock out the seamless studio sweep behind the folded jersey to a transparent PNG lookbook cut-out (outer background only; no interior hole claimed). DELIVERABLE jersey_cutout.png. Consumes the uploaded jersey flat.

TRIAGE BRANCH — the CORRECT treatment for the cap-patch photo. It is a photograph of raised embroidery on fabric, so it is knocked out to a transparent lookbook cut-out, the SAME background-knockout used on the jersey — NOT the trace used on the flat logo sheet. Routing this photo to the tracer would return garbage thread/weave paths. DELIVERABLE cap_patch_cutout.png. Consumes the uploaded cap-patch photo.

chaining_note: Single ingest at step 1 (assets_uploaded); every later step consumes a named prior output. BRAND-PHOTO tributaries converge on one house look: the HERO establishes the target — auto_straighten(2) -> apply_adjustments(3, the authored house grade whose reported temp/tint/exposure/black ARE the shared target) -> adjust_hsl(4, palette) -> select_subject(5) -> masked apply_adjustments(6, subject-only lift) -> add_grain(7)=brand_01 master. Five sibling frames each fan out from assets_uploaded and reason a DIFFERENT correction to the SAME target before the shared grain finish: overcast(8->9), net-cage(10->11, tint correction the others don't need), golden-hour(12->13, warm+exposure-down), open-shade(14->15, strongest warm shift), midday(16->17, highlight recovery + controlled shadow). crop_and_resize(18) reframes the graded hero master into the wide header with owned negative space (card cropped out). LOGO tributary: crop_to_bounds(19, prep) -> vectorize(20)=traced SVG; document_render_vector(21)=vector master PDF and (22)=raster preview both EXPORT the authored .ai (one media type per call). AWAY-CREST tributary: auto_straighten(23) -> crop_to_bounds(24) -> apply_halftone(25)=one-colour separation. MERCH: remove_background(26)=jersey cut-out; TRIAGE remove_background(27)=cap-patch cut-out routed away from the tracer. Six graded masters, one header, one report, two logo exports + one traced SVG, one print separation and two cut-outs all emerge from the chain; no step starts from nothing except the eleven genuine client inputs.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon apparel/brand-identity production pack: 27 dependent connector calls across 12 distinct Adobe tools spanning four groups (asset ingest, raster/Lightroom grade, vector trace + vector-document export, print-FX halftone). Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing: a single asset_add_file ingest (no upload-pair inflation), then genuinely dependent chains. The core is a cross-asset grade-MATCH of six differently-lit frames to one measurable house target (a common white point read off each frame's in-frame grey card and a common near-black floor), which forces NON-identical per-frame corrections — warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed, a green frame tinted, a bright frame pulled down, a contrasty frame highlight-recovered — authored from image_apply_adjustments primitives plus a masked image_adjust_hsl palette move and a masked subject lift, never a preset or auto-tone. Around it sit constraint-reasoning beats: prep-before-trace on the logo sheet; EXPORT-only use of document_render_vector on an authored .ai (not composition); straighten-before-crop-before-halftone on the tilted crest (only auto_straighten rectifies a tilt); an honest gen-free crop reframe for the header (no outpaint/canvas-extend, no upscale from the 4000px master); and a triage of the embroidered cap photo away from the tracer to remove_background. The agent performs NO measurement — it neutralises each grey card by eye and REPORTS the parameters it applied. All 27 steps are headless [C], server=adobe.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (wrong DECISIONS, never a self-measurement).
